Build the system. Survive the day.

Learn system design, one idea at a time

41 free lessons, from requests and caching to consistency, data storage and leading a design discussion. Follow the tracks or choose one idea.

Start

  • 3 minutes

    Your first system

    Build a tiny app in three minutes and keep it standing through a rush of visitors.

  • 3 minutes

    What a request is, and p50 versus p99

    A request is one question and one answer. Averages hide the slow ones that people remember.

  • 3 minutes

    Numbers you can do in your head

    Turn monthly users into requests per second and servers needed, with a pencil.

Scale the front

  • 3 minutes

    Spreading load

    A load balancer hands each request to a free server so none is overwhelmed.

  • 3 minutes

    Remembering answers

    A cache keeps recent answers in memory so the database is asked less.

  • 3 minutes

    Copies near users

    A CDN keeps copies of files and pages close to people, so your servers see far fewer requests.

  • 3 minutes

    Adding servers, and why it is late

    Autoscaling adds servers when busy, but new servers take minutes to start.

Scale the data

  • 3 minutes

    Copies are a little behind

    Read copies share the load, but they trail the original by a moment.

  • 3 minutes

    Splitting data

    When one database cannot take the writes, split the data across several.

  • 3 minutes

    When one item is popular

    Sharding spreads keys, not popularity. One star item can still overload one shard.

  • 3 minutes

    Search is a copy

    A search index is a second copy of your data, shaped for finding words fast.

  • 3 minutes

    Hot, warm, cold and archive

    Old data is rarely read, so keep it somewhere cheaper and slower.

Work later

  • 3 minutes

    Waiting instead of breaking

    A queue lets a burst wait in line instead of crashing the thing behind it.

  • 3 minutes

    One post, millions of feeds

    A post by a celebrity must reach millions of feeds; do it in the background.

  • 3 minutes

    Live sockets and presence

    Chat and live scores keep a connection open; that changes how you count capacity.

Stay correct

  • 3 minutes

    Which copy is the truth

    With several copies, you choose between always-latest and always-fast.

  • 3 minutes

    Exactly once, on purpose

    Retries are normal, so every action must be safe to repeat.

Stay up

  • 3 minutes

    Saying "slow down" politely

    A limit per client stops one noisy caller or a flood from taking everyone down.

  • 3 minutes

    Timeouts and failing fast

    When a dependency is slow, give up early so your servers do not pile up waiting.

  • 4 minutes

    Surviving a region

    A whole region can go dark. Run in two, and send people to the one that is up.

  • 3 minutes

    Seeing problems early

    You cannot fix what you cannot see: metrics, alerts and a way back.

Business

  • 3 minutes

    Where the money goes

    Every box has a monthly price. Good design meets the goal without waste.

  • 3 minutes

    Proof built in

    Auditors want proof: who did what, who can see what, and that data is protected.

  • 3 minutes

    GPUs, tokens and fallbacks

    Serving AI answers is slow and expensive, so cache, limit, and have a fallback.

Go deeper

  • 7 minutes

    Consistent hashing and moving data

    Adding one machine can mean moving a little data or nearly all of it.

  • 7 minutes

    Copies and quorums

    Copies tolerate failures when placement, acknowledgements and repair match the promise.

  • 7 minutes

    Agreeing on one leader

    A leader needs a safe election and a way to stop old owners from acting.

  • 7 minutes

    What consistent really means

    Choose the guarantee for each operation and name what a partition changes.

  • 7 minutes

    Inside a storage engine

    The path from a write to disk decides memory, I/O and cost.

  • 7 minutes

    Work across services

    Make each step durable and show the user what is still pending.

  • 7 minutes

    Ordering and time

    A timestamp can sort events without proving which event caused another.

  • 7 minutes

    Syncing across devices

    Offline edits need durable local intent, a cursor and a plan for old devices.

  • 7 minutes

    Privacy by design

    The safest data to protect is data the service never receives.

  • 7 minutes

    How metrics systems work

    Series count, replication and query work decide the size of a metrics platform.

  • 7 minutes

    Logs and traces

    Keep enough evidence to explain failures without indexing or retaining everything.

  • 7 minutes

    SLOs and error budgets

    Turn a user promise into a budget and an actionable alert.

  • 7 minutes

    Many customers on one system

    Fairness and failure boundaries matter as much as total capacity.

Lead the design

  • 6 minutes

    How to lead a design interview

    Use the hour to make decisions, test assumptions and invite useful disagreement.

  • 7 minutes

    The simplest thing that works

    Include people, failure recovery and future triggers in the cost of a design.

  • 7 minutes

    Changing a running system

    A safe migration preserves compatibility through the whole rollback window.

  • 7 minutes

    Designs that other teams must live with

    A boundary is a contract and an operating responsibility, not just a box.
